problems.title: Convert a number to binary
problems.question: Write 289 in base two.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: Binary digits record which powers of 2 occur.
steps: 289=256+32+1=2⁸+2⁵+2⁰. Put ones in positions 8,5,0 and zeros elsewhere: 100100001₂.

problems.title: Tangent of the middle angle
problems.question: A triangle has sides 5,12,13. Find the tangent of its middle-sized angle.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: $5^2+12^2=13^2$, so it is right; larger sides face larger angles.
steps: The middle angle faces side 12 and has adjacent leg 5. Its tangent is 12/5=2.4.

problems.title: A constant annual percentage increase
problems.question: 1000 GEL grows by 440 GEL in two years at a fixed annual compound rate. Find that annual percentage.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
steps: (1+r)²=1.44, so 1+r=1.2, taking the positive growth multiplier. Thus r=0.2=20%.

problems.title: A product involving quadratic roots
problems.question: x₁,x₂ are roots of x²+20x+5=0. Find (8x₁−1)(8x₂−1).
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
steps: Expand the product as 64x₁x₂−8(x₁+x₂)+1=320+160+1=481.

problems.title: Circumradius of a five-five-six triangle
problems.question: Find the circumradius of a triangle with sides 5,5,6.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
steps: The altitude to base 6 is √(25−9)=4, so area S=6×4/2=12. Radius=5×5×6/(4×12)=25/8.

problems.title: Distance between quadratic roots
problems.question: Find the absolute root difference of 2x²+4x−3=0.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
steps: The discriminant is 16+24=40. Divide √40 by 2 to get √10.

problems.title: Sine from two hypotenuse projections
problems.question: ABC is right at C, CD an altitude, AD:DB=3:4. Find sin A.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
steps: sin²A=DB/AB=4/7. Since A is acute, sin A=2/√7=2√7/7.

steps: Since (u+v)²=64=u²+v²+2uv, subtracting gives uv=64−49=15. The sides 3,5 realize the data.

problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
steps: t²+4t−12=(t−2)(t+6)=0. Only t=2 is positive, giving x=−2,2.

problems.title: Two possible ratios in a nonlinear system
problems.question: x²+2xy=y²+2 and y²−xy=4. Which listed x/y is possible?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: The second equation ensures y≠0; eliminate the constants.
steps: Subtract half the second equation from the first after putting everything on the left. The result is 2x²+5xy−3y²=(2x−y)(x+3y)=0.
Thus x/y=1/2 or −3. Both are feasible because y²(1−x/y)=4 has a positive right-hand solution for y² in each case. Only −3 is listed.
problems.answer: −3 among the choices; possible ratios are 1/2 and −3.

problems.title: A reciprocal substitution yields two quadratics
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of x²/9+36/x²=5(x/3−6/x).
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: Domain x≠0; put $u=x/3-6/x$, giving left side $u^2+4$.
steps: u²−5u+4=0, so u=1 or 4. These give x²−3x−18=0 and x²−12x−18=0.
Both quadratics have two distinct nonzero real roots, with sums 3 and 12. The combined root sum is 15.

problems.title: An incircle fixes an isosceles side
problems.question: BC is the base of isosceles ABC, O is incenter, tan OBC=1/2, and inradius is 3. Find the equal side.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
steps: Let H be the base midpoint. Triangle BOH gives BH=OH/tanα=3/(1/2)=6. The base angle is 2α, so altitude AH=BH·4/3=8.
The equal side AB=√(6²+8²)=10.

problems.title: All nonobtuse triangles with two fixed sides
problems.question: Find x such that sides x,4,5 form a nonobtuse triangle.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: Each side squared must be at most the sum of the other two squared.
steps: 25≤x²+16 requires x≥3. Also x²≤16+25=41 requires x≤√41. The remaining inequality 16≤x²+25 is automatic.
Every x in [3,√41] satisfies the strict triangle inequality 1<x<9. The endpoints give right triangles and are included.

problems.title: Opposite real roots require both sum and sign checks
problems.question: For which listed b does x²+(b²−2b−15)x+b=0 have real roots equal in magnitude and opposite in sign?
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: The root sum must be zero and their product must be negative.
steps: At b=5 the equation x²+5=0 has no real roots. At b=−3 it is x²−3=0, with roots ±√3.

problems.title: Parallelogram perimeter from diagonals and an angle
problems.question: A parallelogram has obtuse angle 120° and diagonals √30,3√2. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
steps: Their sum 48 gives u²+v²=24. Their difference 12 equals 4uv|cos120°|=2uv, so uv=6.
(u+v)²=24+12=36, giving u+v=6 and perimeter 12.

problems.title: A third median from the centroid angle
problems.question: M,N are midpoints of AB,BC. Medians CM=9,AN=6 meet at K, and NKC=60°. Find the third median.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: The centroid divides medians 2:1; vectors from the centroid to the three vertices sum to zero.
steps: CK=6,AK=4, and KA is opposite KN, so AKC=120°. Let a,c be the vertex vectors from K.
The remaining vertex vector is b=−a−c. Thus BK²=16+36+2×4×6 cos120°=28, so BK=2√7.
The full median from B is 3/2 times BK, giving 3√7.

problems.title: Meeting time from two remaining travel times
problems.question: Two cars leave cities 120 km apart toward each other. After meeting, the first arrives in 20 minutes and the second in 80 minutes. Find speed sum.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: If meeting time is T and remaining times t₁,t₂, then $T^2=t_1t_2$.
steps: Before meeting their distances are v₁T,v₂T. Afterwards v₁t₁=v₂T and v₂t₂=v₁T; multiplying gives the formula.
T=√[(1/3)(4/3)]=2/3 hour. Since the cars cover 120 km together before meeting, v₁+v₂=120/(2/3)=180 km/h.

problems.title: An odd number of roots forces zero to be a root
problems.question: Find all a such that (|x|+1)(|x|+2)(|x|−3)(|x|−4)=a²−1 has exactly five distinct real roots.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: Nonzero roots occur in ± pairs, so an odd count requires x=0.
steps: At x=0 the product is 24, forcing a²−1=24, or a=±5. Check sufficiency using t=|x|≥0 and u=t²−2t.
The product is (u−3)(u−8). With right side 24 this gives u(u−11)=0. Allowed t values are 0,2,1+2√3.
They yield x=0,±2,±(1+2√3), exactly five distinct roots.

problems.title: A coefficient sum without expansion
problems.question: (x²−199x+5)(x²+2023x+1)(x+2)²(x−1)=x⁷+ax⁶+bx⁵+cx⁴+dx³+ex²+fx+g. Find a+b+c+d+e+f.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: Evaluate at x=0 for g and at x=1 for the total coefficient sum.
steps: At x=0, g=5×1×4×(−1)=−20. At x=1 the product is zero, so 1+a+b+c+d+e+f+g=0.
The requested sum is −1−g=19.

problems.title: A golden ratio from a thirty-six-degree apex
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has apex B=36°. Find equal-side length divided by a base-angle bisector length.
problems.idea: Apply the relevant formula and check roots, signs and geometric feasibility.
formulas: Base angles are 72°; use isosceles triangles and the angle-bisector theorem.
steps: Let AB=BC=L,AC=b, and AD bisect A. Then BAD=CAD=36°. Triangle ABD has equal angles at A,B, so BD=AD.
Triangle ACD has C=D=72°, so AD=AC=b. Thus BD=b and DC=L−b. The angle-bisector theorem gives b/(L−b)=L/b.
Putting z=L/b gives z²−z−1=0, so z=(1+√5)/2. Since AD=b, this is also L/AD.
